item.title: Version 0.19.1
item.description: • Fixed: re-processing a meeting while its transcript window is open now updates the window in place. Previously the window could show internal placeholder labels (like __speaker) or keep the old speaker layout until you closed and reopened it. This affected every mode switch — Me/Them, No diarization, and full diarization.

item.title: Version 0.19.0
item.description:
• You can now add system audio to a recording that is already running. If a call starts in the middle of a mic-only recording, click SYSTEM in the popover — or accept the prompt Kera shows when it notices the call. The other side is captured from that moment on, and everything stays on one transcript timeline.
  • Fixed a bug where a recording with both mic and system audio could lose most of the system side from the transcript when the two tracks needed alignment.
  • The "system audio was recorded silent" warning now judges the system track itself, not the length of the whole recording, so it can no longer flag a track that simply started late.
  • Kera no longer warns about blocked system audio before a call has started.

item.title: Version 0.18.3 — Choose how a meeting is re-processed
item.description:
What changed

  • New Reprocess options setting under Settings → About → Developer. Turn it on and re-processing a meeting asks which transcription service and diarization method to use, instead of silently reusing whichever one the meeting was originally made with.
  • That picker already existed, but could only be switched on by typing a hidden command into Terminal—so it quietly vanished the moment you moved to a new Mac. It is now a normal setting that follows you.
  • If you had already enabled it by hand, nothing changes: the setting shows as on and keeps working.

item.title: Version 0.18.2 — Reliable system audio recording
item.description:
What changed

  • Kera now asks for macOS System Audio Recording permission. Without that grant the audio tap does not fail—it records pure silence—so meetings could complete with the other participants missing entirely from the recording.
  • The setup checklist now checks System Audio Recording directly, and the Screen Recording row explains what it actually does: detecting which app is holding a meeting.
  • If no sound reaches Kera from the meeting app during the first minute, you are warned while the meeting is still running rather than discovering it afterward. Recording continues, and your microphone track is kept intact.

item.title: Version 0.18.1 — Exact people search and a faster library
item.description:
What changed

  • Click a participant or choose a person suggestion in Library search to show only calls where that person is an actual resolved speaker—not merely mentioned in a title or transcript.
  • Search for people from the meeting list, transcript reader, or Speakers Library, with a compact person icon that makes the active filter clear.
  • Enjoy a more responsive Library and Speakers experience through safer catalog reuse and fewer redundant refreshes.
  • Credential editing and background refreshes are now more resilient to temporary Keychain errors.

item.title: Version 0.18.0 — Faster long meetings, smoother playback, safer recording
item.description:
This is a focused performance and reliability release. The biggest improvements show up in long recordings, large transcripts, and meeting detection running throughout the day.

What changed

  • Long recordings use dramatically less memory. Preparing combined microphone and system audio used about 95% less memory in our 30-minute benchmark—dropping from roughly 727 MB to 38 MB—and remained near 50 MB for a three-hour recording.
  • Speaker separation does less repeated work. Kera now decodes local audio once, reuses it for voice checks, and avoids repeatedly scanning every transcript and speaker segment. Long, speaker-heavy recordings should finish with lower memory use and better scaling, without changing the existing speaker-assignment rules.
  • Large transcripts play more smoothly. The Transcript Reader now builds its playback timeline only when its content changes, instead of rebuilding it continuously during playback. Scrolling, highlighting, and screenshot timelines stay responsive even in very large meetings.
  • Meeting detection is quieter and more reliable. Kera wakes for relevant app events instead of polling four times per second. Browser and native-app checks now have real deadlines, and an unresponsive or permission-blocked check is treated as uncertain rather than falsely deciding that your call ended.
  • Microphone capture is more resilient. Audio conversion and file writing now happen away from the real-time microphone path, reducing the risk of glitches under load. Pause, stop, device changes, and write failures are handled more carefully, and Kera reports capture failures instead of silently dropping audio. Transcription now starts only after recording metadata is safely on disk, so a disk-full recording remains recoverable instead of disappearing from the Library.

item.title: Version 0.17.2 — Faster libraries and safer transcription recovery
item.description:
What changed

  • Recent Meetings and Speakers Library are substantially faster on large histories. Kera now maintains a rebuildable SQLite read cache, avoiding repeated parsing of every transcript whenever these surfaces refresh.
  • Your recordings stay as normal files. meta.json, transcripts, and audio remain the source of truth; there is no database migration or lock-in. If the cache is missing or damaged, Kera rebuilds it automatically and can fall back to the existing file scanner.
  • Storage cleanup remains fully supported. Size accounting, tidy, WAV-to-M4A compression, remove-audio, and automatic cleanup still operate directly on recording files. The cache follows compression and audio-removal changes, and Storage refreshes when the recordings folder changes.
  • Recoverable transcription failures now surface immediately. When the audio is still intact, Kera shows the failed recording in Library, offers retry or on-device Local transcription, and provides an Open Library notification instead of leaving the session stranded on disk.

On a 453-folder library, an unchanged catalog refresh measured about 67 ms; loading 424 Recent rows measured about 8 ms.

item.title: Version 0.17.1 — Crash fix
item.description: • Fixed a crash that could happen right after updating when Kera resumed diarizing a queued recording whose detected speaker segments were all too short/noisy and got cleaned away. Kera now treats that as an empty diarization result instead of crashing.

item.title: Version 0.17.0
item.description:
What's new

Speaker tagging autocompletes names from your library. Start typing a name and Kera filters your saved people live — press Tab to fill in the top match. Works everywhere you tag: the one-at-a-time card, the inline row, and the rename popover.

Fixes

  • Playing a speaker sample right after tagging the previous one no longer cuts out after a split second.
  • Voice Memos import now shows your most recent recordings — including ones still downloading from iCloud, which appear marked "Not downloaded" instead of going missing.
  • Added a Refresh button to the Voice Memos import window so new recordings show up without reopening it.

item.title: Version 0.16.0
item.description:
Quiet audio no longer goes missing from transcripts. Recordings with quiet stretches — audio played from a phone into your mic, or a call where the mic was turned down — could lose whole sections before transcription. Kera now adapts to each recording's own levels, so quiet speech gets transcribed instead of silently disappearing. A new safety guard also makes sure a quiet recording is never mistaken for silence and trimmed down — your audio is always kept.

FaceTime & Phone (experimental) now capture the other side. With the experimental FaceTime / macOS Phone detection enabled, Kera records the other person's audio too — the system-audio track used to come up empty.

item.title: Version 0.15.0
item.description:
Detect more call apps (experimental). FaceTime, the macOS Phone app, WhatsApp, Slack, and Signal can now be detected as calls — opt-in under a new Experimental section in Settings → Recording. They're off by default while detection is being verified (an unverified detector can occasionally mis-fire and start a recording when there's no call). Turn one on to try it.

Design polish. Badges, the first-run permissions screen, and other surfaces moved onto the IBM Plex type system for a more consistent look.

item.title: Version 0.14.0
item.description:
• Voice Memos import — import recordings straight from the macOS Voice Memos app (menu bar → Import Audio → From Voice Memos). Pick from your memo list, or choose files manually.
  • Recording now keeps going when you connect, disconnect, or switch your microphone (e.g. AirPods) mid-recording, instead of stopping.

item.title: Version 0.13.5
item.description:
• Instant "No diarization" reprocessing — Switching an already-transcribed call to No-diarization mode is now instant. Kera reuses the existing transcript instead of re-processing the audio, so there's no cloud round-trip or wait.
  • Cleaner transcript exports — Exported transcripts for No-diarization recordings no longer show an internal speaker placeholder.

item.title: Version 0.13.4
item.description:
Browser calls now record both sides

Google Meet — and other browser-based calls (Chrome, Arc, Edge, Brave, and similar) — now correctly capture the other participants' audio, not just your microphone. Previously these calls recorded your mic only, leaving the far side silent.

Kera also now flags a recording, both live and right after it ends, if system audio isn't being captured — so a silent recording can't slip by unnoticed.

item.title: Version 0.13.3
item.description:
What's new in 0.13.3

A hardening pass over the new recording HUD, focused on making the stream-health indicators trustworthy.

NO SIGNAL you can trust

  • The red NO SIGNAL warning now means exactly one thing: Kera stopped receiving that audio stream. Being muted, listening quietly, or pausing the recording no longer triggers it — sustained quiet just dims that side of the waveform instead.
  • Stream health is tracked for the whole recording, even while the popover is closed — if a stream dies mid-call, the warning is already showing the moment you open it.
  • If an audio stream stops delivering, its waveform now honestly flatlines instead of freezing on the last activity.
  • Mic-only recordings no longer warn about missing system audio — there's none by design, and the legend shows that calmly.

Mid-recording engine picker, safer

  • Soniox can't be selected without an API key configured — the option is disabled with a hint instead of letting a recording finish unprocessable. If the key disappears mid-recording, Kera falls back to on-device transcription rather than failing your meeting.

Under the hood

  • Recordings that lose their mic stream keep accurate duration metadata.
  • Removed repeated Keychain lookups from the popover's render loop.

item.title: Version 0.13.2
item.description:
What's new in 0.13.2

Recording HUD

  • Change your mind mid-recording — the mode (FULL DIAR) and engine (LOCAL / SONIOX) labels in the recording popover are now clickable. Pick a different diarization mode or transcription engine while the call is still going; the change applies when you stop, and the live recording is never interrupted.
  • See both audio streams — the waveform now shows your mic above the line and system audio below it, each in its own color. If a stream stops delivering audio mid-call, its side flattens and a red NO SIGNAL warning appears — so a dead mic can't go unnoticed again.
  • Smoother start/stop — starting a recording now morphs the Start button into Stop in place. The popover keeps a constant size, so nothing jumps or wiggles.

Transcripts

  • Find in transcript (⌘F) — search any transcript with match highlighting, a result counter, and Enter / ⌘G to jump between matches. Works during playback.

Reliability

  • Recordings no longer get stuck as "failed" when the microphone stream dies mid-session — Kera now protects the captured audio and recovers using whichever stream is healthy on retry.
  • Safari meeting detection fixed — it was silently broken for Safari tabs.
  • Browser detection respects your choices — if you turned off browser meeting detection, updates can no longer quietly re-enable it for newly supported browsers. Title-based detection (Firefox and friends) now tells you in Settings when it needs Screen Recording permission.
  • Tighter Google Meet tab matching, so ordinary pages with "Meet" in the title can't trigger a phantom meeting.

Settings

  • Your AI naming key is kept per provider — switching providers no longer loses what you typed, and clearing the field now actually removes the stored key.

item.title: Version 0.13.1
item.description:
Meeting detection in any browser

  • Fixed: Google Meet and Teams calls in Arc were not being detected. Arc handles automation requests differently from Chrome, which left the tab scan silently empty — detection now reads tabs in a way every browser answers, and it's faster too.
  • Detection now works in any browser. Chrome, Arc, Dia, Edge, Brave, Vivaldi, Opera and Safari are detected through their tabs; Firefox — and any browser Kera doesn't know by name — is covered through its window title. One toggle in Settings → Recording covers them all.

item.title: Version 0.13.0
item.description:
Storage management

  • Compress audio — re-encode meetings to compact m4a at about a tenth of the size. Everything still plays, re-processes, and splits; only lossless fidelity is lost. One click compresses your whole library, with an honest estimate up front and real numbers after.
  • New Storage section in Settings — see exactly what's on disk (audio vs transcripts), tidy up leftover working files, and remove audio from older or larger meetings while keeping their transcripts, summaries, and screenshots searchable.
  • Automatic cleanup (optional, off by default) — compress or remove meeting audio automatically after 30/60/90 days. Recently imported recordings always get the full grace period.
  • Meetings whose audio was removed stay fully readable everywhere, with clear "transcript only" labeling instead of broken buttons.

Meeting detection

  • Microsoft Teams calls are now detected by their actual call audio, not window titles — detection works in fullscreen, on other Spaces, and with meetings joined by phone audio. Incoming ringtones no longer trigger false detections.
  • Detection rides out short audio-system hiccups mid-call instead of declaring the meeting over.
  • New per-app detection toggles in Settings → Recording.

Reliability

  • If the disk fills up or audio can't be written mid-recording, Kera now stops safely and tells you — instead of showing a green light over a silently truncated file.
  • Quitting Kera while recording now finalizes the recording cleanly.

Library

  • Double-click a meeting to open it.
  • Right-click any meeting to regenerate its summary.
  • Storage numbers now match what Finder reports.
  • Many fixes across speaker retagging, voice profile recovery, and transcript processing.

item.title: Version 0.12.18
item.description:
Screenshots, pinned to your transcript

  • Capture a screenshot during a recording and it’s pinned to the transcript

at the exact moment you took it. Press ⌃⇧S (or the camera button in the menu-bar recording controls), drag a region — or press Space to grab a window — and it shows up inline in the transcript later. Tap it to jump to that moment, hover to enlarge. The shortcut is configurable in Settings → Shortcuts.

Kera learns voices as you name them

  • Naming an unrecognized speaker now teaches Kera that voice. Type someone’s

name on an unknown speaker and a voice profile is created from that meeting — so Kera recognizes them automatically in future meetings instead of leaving them unlabeled.

  • Catch up your existing people: the Speakers Library now has a

“Create voice profile from a meeting” button for anyone who’s only ever been a typed label. One click builds their profile from a past meeting.

Fixes

  • The “Record this meeting?” prompt now appears immediately when you start a

new meeting right after stopping a previous one (it used to lag by up to a minute).

item.title: Version 0.12.17
item.description:
Long recordings no longer fail silently

Recordings longer than 5 hours exceed the cloud transcriber's limit. Kera now detects this automatically and transcribes them on your Mac instead, so a long import or meeting always ends with a transcript.

Failed transcriptions are now recoverable

If a transcription fails — a file that's too long, a dropped network, or a cloud hiccup — the recording now shows at the top of your Library with one-click Retry, Transcribe locally (on-device), Dismiss, and Delete. Previously a failed recording disappeared with no way to get it back.

item.title: Version 0.12.16
item.description: Fixed: Import from Plaud was failing with an "unexpected response" error and an unhelpful Retry button. Plaud changed how its web sign-in returns your login token, and Kera was reading the old (now-empty) value — so every import attempt went out unauthenticated. Kera now reads the token from its new location, and Import from Plaud works again.

item.title: Version 0.12.15
item.description:
Speaker photos

  • Give any speaker a photo in the Speakers window — drag an image onto their avatar, or click to choose one. Their photo then appears everywhere they show up: meeting rows, participant lists, and the transcript.
  • Photos follow a person through renames and merges, and Undo restores a photo if you change your mind.

A calmer meeting library

  • The meeting list is quieter: the two-line summary preview now shows only on the selected meeting, with clear "summarizing…" and "summary failed" states on the others.
  • The detail pane is consolidated around one primary action plus an overflow menu, with a title-led header.
  • The filter pills (All · This week · Month · Needs tagging) now stay on a single line instead of wrapping.

Simpler meeting splitting

  • "Split this meeting" is now a clean list of the meetings Kera detected, with one-tap Merge to combine two and Remove to drop one. The meeting count and the button always reflect exactly what you'll get.
  • Splitting now happens after import, where the transcript makes detection more accurate.

Speaker tagging

  • When a speaker's auto-picked voice sample is unclear, Try another sample lets you audition a few other clips and choose the clearest one.

item.title: Version 0.12.14
item.description:
New

Import from Plaud — Bring recordings from your Plaud device straight into Kera. When a single recording actually holds several back-to-back meetings, Kera spots the breaks and offers to split it into separate meetings on import — each with its own transcript and summary.

Split a meeting — Turn one long meeting into several. Kera suggests where the topics change and proposes a title for each part; you can fine-tune the cuts on an editable timeline before committing. Every resulting meeting gets its own summary. Changed your mind? Restore brings the original back. Available anywhere you manage a meeting — the library list (right-click), the meeting detail view, and the transcript window.

Improved

  • New recordings now trim leading and trailing silence automatically.
  • Preparing a split shows an "Analyzing transcript…" indicator, so it's clear Kera is working while it finds the topic boundaries.

item.title: Version 0.12.13
item.description:
What's new

  • Rename meetings directly from the Meeting Library title and from recording context menus.
  • Manual meeting titles now persist across speaker edits, reprocessing, auto-title updates, and app refreshes.
  • Renaming a meeting also renames its backing session folder and updates derived artifacts/index entries safely.
  • The menubar popover now opens immediately instead of waiting on a cold full recents scan, with async recents refresh and lightweight loading feedback.

Fixes

  • Improved cache invalidation and refresh behavior around recording metadata changes.
  • Added safeguards for session-folder moves during background transcription/finalization paths.

item.title: Version 0.12.12
item.description:
NEW — Waveform reflects both mic and system audio

The live waveform in the recording popover now responds to both microphone input AND system audio (when a call app like Zoom is being tapped), not just to the mic. During a call where the other side is doing the talking, the waveform now moves with them — useful as a real-time signal that audio is actually being captured.

If you record a call and the waveform only moves when you talk while the other side is clearly audible in your headphones, that's a sign the per-process system-audio tap is silently capturing zeros — open Settings → Send Diagnostics and share the zip with support.

FIXED — Bars no longer poke above the row on loud audio

The waveform bars are clamped to the row height. Loud system audio (music share, shared YouTube playback) used to occasionally clip above the container; that's resolved.

FIXED — "Microphone + app" label is honest on tap failure

If system-audio capture fails to start (e.g. Screen Recording permission denied), the label in the recording popover now falls back to just "Microphone" instead of misleadingly showing the call app's name while no system audio is actually being recorded.

item.title: Version 0.12.11
item.description:
NEW — Silent system-audio warning

If a recording's system.wav comes back effectively silent (the file is the right size, but audiotee captured zeros — a real macOS routing edge case that hits a handful of users), the session row now shows a small orange warning triangle. The tooltip points you at **Settings → Send Diagnostics** and mentions that virtual audio drivers (Loopback / BlackHole / Audio Hijack) are an expected cause — those intercept audio before Kera's per-process tap can capture it.

CHANGED — Zoom detection rework

The Zoom in-call detector no longer relies on window-title scraping alone. The primary signal is now CoreAudio's per-process audio activity flags (macOS 14.4+). That fixes:

  • The "Meeting Detected … Meeting Ended" flap a few seconds into real

Zoom calls, which was firing the "Save / Discard" prompt mid-call.

  • False-positive sticky "Meeting Detected" state after the call ended

(Zoom leaves a Personal Meeting Room preview window open whose title doesn't match the in-call pattern).

Settings → Advanced has a zoomDetectAudioState kill-switch that falls back to title-only detection if needed.

CHANGED — Send Diagnostics now bundles audio-environment context

The diagnostics zip now also contains a point-in-time snapshot of the machine's audio environment — devices, HAL-registered audio processes, installed third-party HAL plugins (BlackHole etc.), TCC status for mic and screen recording, coreaudiod's own log, and a few related signals. Privacy-safe scalar audio-health stats (RMS, peak, silence fraction) are also stored per session.

The bundle stays opt-in: nothing auto-uploads, no audio content, no transcript content. Send Diagnostics also shows "Generating…" on the button while the bundle is being built so you can tell it's working.

FIXED — Safari/Chrome/Arc tab scanner survives huge tab sets

The browser-tab scanner used by the meeting detector now wraps each window's tab enumeration in its own try block, so a tab closing between the "list windows" and "list tabs" steps no longer aborts the whole scan. Stress-tested against 234 open tabs in Arc.

FIXED — Audio file picker no longer launches with the menubar host inactive

NSApp.activate(ignoringOtherApps: true) is now called before NSOpenPanel.runModal() in the menubar host, so the import-audio picker shows up in the foreground instead of behind whatever app was active.

FIXED — cut.sh drops root cleanly when triggered remotely

The orchestrator path was leaving the inner shell at EUID=0, which poisoned .git/objects/ on every git operation. The wrapper now uses sudo launchctl asuser 501 su -m yonibloch -c '…' so git/Xcode ops run as the real user.

item.title: Version 0.12.10
item.description:
Fixed — "Meeting detected" prompt no longer re-fires after you skip it

If you dismissed the floating "Meeting detected · Zoom" prompt and your meeting kept going, the prompt would re-appear within seconds — sometimes over and over until you quit the app to escape. That bug is now fixed.

Root cause: a single transient detection flicker (Zoom going fullscreen, browser tab title refresh, helper-process restart) unconditionally cleared the "user already said no" state. Kera now requires 5 consecutive no-meeting ticks (~15 seconds) before considering a dismissal stale — so flickers don't undo your Skip.

New — Send Diagnostics

Settings → About → Diagnostics → Send Diagnostics: produces a .zip you can attach to a bug report. Inside:

  • Kera + macOS + hardware version info
  • Last 30 minutes of Kera's OSLog
  • Your Settings (UserDefaults)
  • Sparkle auto-updater state
  • The last 5 sessions' meta.json manifests

Each zip includes a README.txt explaining what's in it and what's deliberately omitted. No transcripts, no audio, no API keys. Nothing auto-uploads — you write it to disk and choose where to send it.

Under the hood

553 tests now pass (was 543 in v0.12.9 — 11 new tests for the diagnostics bundle, including an end-to-end smoke test that drives the real /usr/bin/log and /usr/bin/zip).

item.title: Version 0.12.9
item.description:
NEW — Transcript export folder

Settings → Recording → Storage has a new top row: **Transcript export folder**. When you set it, Kera writes a Markdown copy of every transcript there, with YAML frontmatter and a stable filename:

``` 2026-05-13 — Sprint Planning [a1b2c3].md ```

Use it to feed Obsidian, Notion, Drive, a grep-able archive, or anything else that wants plain Markdown. The setting is optional — leave it as "Off" and nothing changes from prior versions.

Details:

  • Re-exports automatically whenever the transcript changes

(finalize, speaker edits, reprocess, bulk speaker rename) — your Markdown copy stays in sync with what Kera shows in the Reader.

  • Filenames are deterministic: same session re-exports always

overwrite the same file. Cross-session collisions on date+title use the [hex6] suffix from the session ID to stay unique.

  • Don't hand-edit the exported .md — Kera may overwrite it on the

next speaker/title change. If you want stable annotations, copy the file out of the export folder first.

  • Renaming a meeting title leaves the old filename behind as an

orphan; the new title gets a new file. Delete the orphan by hand if it bugs you.

  • YAML titles are sanitized for safety (interior newlines, line

separators, illegal filename chars are stripped) — pasted titles with weird characters don't break the frontmatter.

Recordings folder picker — renamed, demoted

The picker that v0.12.7/0.12.8 added under "Transcripts folder" controlled both recordings AND transcripts (it's actually the library root). That naming was misleading — moved this version:

  • Renamed to "Recordings folder" and tucked under a new

"Advanced" disclosure in Settings → Recording → Storage.

  • Most people should never touch it; it stays on the default

~/Library/Application Support/Kera/recordings.

  • Existing custom values still work — your recordings stay where

you put them. If you picked a custom folder previously thinking it was for transcripts only, expand "Advanced" to see/change it.

Under the hood

This shipped after 7 rounds of rival-panel plan hardening and 4 rounds of rival-panel review hardening. 543 tests now pass (was 516 before the export-folder work).

item.title: Version 0.12.8
item.description:
Storage folder is now configurable

Settings → Recording → Storage lets you pick where Kera saves new transcripts and recordings. The default is unchanged (~/Library/Application Support/Kera/recordings); pick any folder you have write access to (Documents, an external SSD, anywhere) and new sessions land there.

  • The picker validates the folder is writable before it sticks — if it's

read-only or unreachable, you get a clear error instead of a confusing recording failure later.

  • Folder is locked while a recording is in progress — change it from a

clean idle state.

  • Existing recordings don't move. Switching folders just changes where

new sessions land; old ones stay where they were until you move them in Finder.

  • The menubar popover and Speakers Library refresh themselves

automatically when you change folders — no app restart needed.

item.title: Version 0.12.7
item.description:
Configurable bullet threshold

The 30-min hardcoded cutoff for bulleted summaries is now a setting. Settings → AI naming + summaries → "Bullet points for meetings longer than" — slider with 7 stops: Never · 15+ · 30+ · 45+ · 60+ · 90+ · Every meeting. Default stays at 30 min, so existing behavior is preserved unless you move the slider.

Menubar popover redesign

Both the idle and live-recording cells now use the same calmer type system as the rest of the app — no more 32pt "Ready" / 26pt "Microphone" hero shouting over the recent rows.

  • Status word renders at 15pt/600 (same as a recent-row title)
  • Eyebrow line uses the standard keraSectionEyebrow modifier
  • Primary CTA is a pill button (ink-fill idle, red-fill live, paper text) instead of a bold-underline link
  • Live cell: pause/stop are stacked pill CTAs in the right column; audio meter loses its black border and renders as a borderless inline waveform

Idle ↔ live now feel like the same hero with only color changing — eyebrow flips to red, primary fill flips to red.

Backfill modal honest about what'll run

The "Summarize past meetings" modal used to say "Summarize 5 past meetings" while the button below said "Summarize 0 meetings (~$0.00)" when none of the candidates had transcript content. Header now matches the actionable count throughout. Empty-transcript meetings are filtered out before they reach the runner, so they no longer get marked .failed after a backfill — the modal's "skipped" promise is now honest.

When nothing is actionable, the modal flips to "Nothing to summarize" with explanatory copy and a single Close button.

Other fixes

  • Return no longer stops a recording. The Stop button on the live popover used to bind to ⏎, same as the idle Start button — meaning a user reopening the popover during a meeting and hitting Return out of muscle memory would silently kill the session. Click-only now for the destructive primary.
  • Detail-pane summary wraps to its full height instead of clipping mid-sentence with empty space below (SwiftUI layout fix).
  • Detail pane anchors the meeting title + Open transcript / Reprocess / Copy / Summarize buttons; only the Summary section scrolls.
  • Policy decoder clamps corrupted UserDefaults values so a stray defaults write can't poison tier dispatch.

item.title: Version 0.12.6
item.description:
Length-aware AI summaries

The big change: long meetings now get richer summaries automatically.

  • Meetings ≤30 min keep the existing 2-3 sentence narrative — same shape as before.
  • Meetings >30 min add a 3-6 bullet list under the narrative. Specific decisions, action items with owners, key context — laid out so a long meeting summary actually reads like a briefing.
  • Library list-row + menubar previews are unchanged on long meetings (still show the narrative); bullets only appear in the detail pane.

The 220-char hard cap that was clipping 71% of summaries is gone — replaced by a 1200-char ceiling for narratives that acts as a runaway-output guard rather than a normal limit.

Reprocess any meeting to regenerate against the new format.

Detail pane polish

  • Header + actions stay anchored on scroll. The title, Open transcript, Reprocess, Copy, and Summarize buttons no longer scroll out of view on long summaries.
  • Summary text wraps to its full height instead of being cut off mid-sentence with empty space below it (a SwiftUI layout fix).

Other fixes

  • Meeting-detect no longer relaunches Safari / Chrome / Arc after you quit them.
  • 37 small UI consistency fixes across the action menu, badges, modals, and selection chrome.
  • Modal scrim is now actually blurred (was rendering as a flat tint).

item.title: Version 0.12.5
item.description:
What changed

  • package-dmg + runbook: KERA_HEADLESS_DMG=1 unlocks SSH-driven cuts
  • cut.sh + runbook: catch missing-Xcode at prereqs, drop OAuth-test fiction
  • docs(release): capture lessons from first real cut on the mini

item.title: Version 0.12.4
item.description:
What changed

  • cut.sh: 1 fix from /ultra round 6 (notes cleanup on resume)
  • cut.sh: 4 fixes from /ultra round 5 (OpenAI's late catches)
  • cut.sh + runbook: 5 fixes from /ultra round 4
  • cut.sh + runbook: 6 fixes from /ultra round 3
  • cut.sh + runbook: 7 fixes from /ultra round 2
  • cut.sh + runbook: 11 fixes from /ultra round 1
  • cut.sh: 6 fixes from rival review

item.title: Version 0.12.3 — Stop the orphan-salvage scanner from deleting crashed recordings
item.description:
Critical data-loss hotfix on top of 0.12.2

The orphan-session scanner that runs at every launch — the mechanism designed to recover recordings from crashes — was itself deleting crashed recordings. The trigger is exact: a SIGABRT crash leaves mic.wav with an unfinalized RIFF/data-chunk-size header (Swift's dealloc never runs to patch them). On next launch, OrphanSessionSalvage called AVAudioFile(forReading:), got length=0 back, the if dur < 5 auto-remove guard fired, and the entire session dir was silently removeItem'd.

If 0.12.2 fixed the crash you were seeing on Zoom disconnect — but you launched 0.12.2 with a crashed recording from 0.12.1 still on disk — that recording was destroyed by 0.12.2's launch sequence. This release fixes that.

Two independent guards now sit between the scanner and your data:

  • Duration estimate falls back to file size. All Kera mic recordings are 16 kHz mono Int16 = 32,000 bytes/sec. When AVAudioFile can't read the unfinalized header, the byte-count estimate kicks in and yields a real duration. A 56-min recording reports as ~3358s instead of 0s.
  • Hard size guard on the auto-remove path. The scanner refuses to delete any file larger than ~200 KB regardless of computed duration. If the duration math ever regresses again, the size gate alone keeps the data on disk so the orphan banner can surface it.

Two regression tests pin the new behavior — one with the exact SIGABRT-truncated WAV shape (RIFF size 0, data chunk size 0), one with a malformed-header large file as belt-and-braces.

If you've already lost a recording to this bug, this release does not bring it back. The file was unlinked, not Trashed, and won't survive without an external backup. Sorry.

item.title: Version 0.12.2 — Mic capture crash hotfix (Zoom disconnect)
item.description:
Hotfix: app no longer aborts when an audio session ends mid-recording

If you were recording while a Zoom call (or any process holding the audio device — Meet, FaceTime, AirPods reconnect, USB mic unplug) released its grip, Kera could die with SIGABRT and lose the in-flight recording. AVAudioEngine was throwing an Objective-C NSException from installTap during the route-flux rebuild, and Swift can't catch ObjC exceptions — so the throw became a hard process abort.

The rebuild path now passes format: nil to installTap, which lets AVAudioEngine introspect the bus state itself at install time and pick a self-consistent format. By construction, the format-mismatch race that caused the crash can't fire on this path. Apple-documented safe form for the API.

If you have a recording that was lost to this crash on 0.12.1, the existing v0.9.49 orphan-session banner picks it up automatically on next launch — click Process to recover the audio that survived (mic.wav writes incrementally to disk; SIGABRT doesn't roll those writes back).

Behind the scenes

  • Test isolation for the keychain. swift test can no longer write to your real login keychain — a structural seam (in-memory provider auto-selected when XCTest is loaded) plus a fail-closed guard on every keychain-touching test. Closes the historical bug where the backfill test suite was overwriting the user's real Anthropic API key on every test run.
  • Defensive empty-write guard. KeychainHelper.set with an empty value now logs a notice and refuses to write — protects against any future code path that could silently blank an API key. Use delete(service:) to intentionally clear.
  • CI on every push. A GitHub Actions workflow now runs swift test on every push to main and every PR. 476 tests, ~30-60s per run with cache.

The deeper hardening of the audio path — small ObjC @try/@catch bridge so any residual AVFoundation exception funnels into the existing markBroken() path instead of aborting, plus tighter format pre-validation — is planned for a follow-up release. This hotfix addresses the known crash trigger; the bridge is belt-and-braces against unknown future variants.

item.title: Version 0.12.1 — Speaker Editor rename now names the meeting
item.description:
If a recording finalized without a meeting name (calendar lookup missed, AI title generator failed, all remote speakers collapsed to the fallback), the Speaker Editor previously couldn't repair it. Labeling SPEAKER_01 as "Uri Vardi" updated the transcript but left the meeting nameless and the folder slug raw.

This release closes that gap. When you label an unknown speaker:

  • Empty meeting_name → composed from scratch. "Call with Uri Vardi", or "Call with Uri Vardi (Sprint Planning)" if a calendar title exists, or "Call with Uri Vardi (My AI Title)" when the LLM-generated title was stored in ai_title.
  • Distinct second rename extends the name. Label SPEAKER_01 → Alice, then SPEAKER_02 → Bob → "Call with Alice, Bob". The second label was silently no-op'ing before.
  • Stale auto-names are cleared. Mark the last remote speaker as non-speech with no calendar/AI title → meeting goes back to nameless rather than freezing on the now-incorrect "Call with Alice".
  • AI-generated parentheticals survive renames. Previously a rename silently dropped the (My AI Title) suffix.
  • Manual free-text titles are protected. "Call with my dentist" is preserved by the strict pre-edit canonical match — only auto-composed names get rewritten.

Folder slug on disk still doesn't auto-update — that needs a system-wide URL invalidation notification (deferred to a future release). 14 new tests, 465 total.

item.title: Version 0.12 — Backfill flow + word-level highlighting on local + Hebrew detect fix
item.description:
Backfill Flow — bulk-summarize past meetings

Enable AI Naming with a backlog of un-summarized meetings? You'll see a banner in Settings → AI Naming offering to "Summarize all" past meetings. The flow:

  • Banner in Settings → AI Naming when un-summarized count > 0. "Not now" dismisses; resurfaces when count grows by 10+ past dismissal.
  • Confirm modal with a live cost estimate (tokens × your provider's pricing). Disabled until the estimate loads.
  • Ambient progress — chip in Settings + footer strip in Library while the bulk runner walks the un-summarized set, 4-wide concurrent.
  • End-of-batch toast: "All caught up." (clean, auto-dismiss 6s) or "Retry failed / Show failed" (partial, manual dismiss). "Show failed" activates a Library filter.

Word-level highlighting on the local engine

WhisperKit-transcribed sessions now carry per-word timing data through to the Transcript Reader, so the active word highlights as audio plays — no more linear interpolation across whole segments. Click anywhere in the transcript to seek to that exact word. The "Word-level sync available" banner stops firing on new local recordings (it only appears now on older sessions that predate this fix).

Diarization on the local engine also benefits: BleedFilter's per-token speaker-assignment path activates, so when two speakers share a Whisper segment, each word goes to whichever speaker the diarizer says is active at that word's start time — replacing the previous winner-take-all overlap voting.

Hebrew language detection: now returns the right default

detectLanguage was returning ("en", 0) on all-Hebrew audio — a meaningless default that runtime had been quietly papering over via the fraction > 0.5 gate. Now correctly returns ("he", 0) on every short-circuit path (model load failure, audio < 10s, no voiced windows above the RMS threshold, any thrown error).

Bundles all of v0.10.5 (Local Me/Them + BleedFilter word-overlap rewrite) and v0.11 (AI Naming sidebar truncation) for users on auto-update jumping straight from v0.10.4.x → v0.12. 445 tests passing.

item.title: Version 0.11 — Local Me/Them + BleedFilter word-overlap + sidebar fix
item.description:
Local Me/Them — WhisperKit-backed, no Soniox required

Me/Them mode (the Me-vs-everyone-else two-bucket transcript) used to require a Soniox API key. v0.11 ships a local Me/Them pipeline that runs natively on WhisperKit — pick Local + Me / Them in the re-process popover and the worker dispatches to the new dual-stream local pipeline.

  • Two sequential WhisperKit transcribes on mic + system, plus per-stream language detection with a 10s duration gate (a noisy short mic stream can't override the meeting language).
  • Heartbeat status during transcribe — "Transcribing microphone (1:30)…" ticks every 15s instead of a frozen string.
  • Calendar attendees drive the "Me + N others" header; degrades cleanly to "Me + others" when no calendar match.
  • Watchdog raised to 6× audio duration for the local Me/Them path (was 3× for full-diar local).

BleedFilter: word-overlap replaces temporal overlap

The previous bleed detection (Detection B) discarded mic activity with >50% temporal overlap with system speech, regardless of text. On Whisper's coarse 10–30s segments, that meant any user interjection during continuous remote speech got dropped as "bleed" — even when the user said something completely different.

The new rule asks the semantically correct question: did the mic capture the same words the system was playing? — by computing a lowercased token-set overlap. True echo (high word overlap) still discards. Distinct parallel speech now survives.

  • Real-audio validation: on a 13-minute Hebrew call, ~26% of "Me" segments survive that would have been silently discarded under the old rule.
  • Affects both backends — Soniox path got the same fix incidentally. The blindspot existed before but was usually masked by Soniox's >0.8s silence-gap cut rule.
  • Detection A (text-equality within ±5s) is unchanged — true echo still caught.

Settings sidebar — AI Naming label fully fixed

Three commits, one chain:

  • Non-breaking space glues "AI Naming" to the ampersand so "&" doesn't widow on its own line.
  • Top-aligned icon + badge with the label capped at 2 lines.
  • Final fix: dropped the Spacer() between the label and the badge in favor of .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading) directly on the Text. The previous layout left only ~83pt for the label, which the medium-weight selected state edged past — truncating "Summaries" to "Summaries…". The new layout gives ~91pt, enough for "AI Naming &" on line 1 with "Summaries" alone on line 2 in either selected or deselected state.

  • Settings sidebar — "AI Naming & Summaries" no longer wraps to a 3-line widow; ampersand glued to "Naming" via non-breaking space.

item.title: Version 0.10.4.2 — Settings polish + language-detection default-on
item.description:
Settings UI consistency + language-detection default-on

v0.10.4 introduced the chrome system but left four .pickerStyle(.segmented) controls inside Settings still painting in system blue. This patch migrates all four to the canonical KeraSegmented component (matching the Library and Speakers Library filter pills): Engine (Local / Soniox), Speaker separation (Local / Cloud), AI Naming Provider (OpenAI / Anthropic), Theme (System / Light / Dark).

SwiftUI .tint(Color.kerInk) propagates from the Settings root, flipping every Toggle's on-state from system blue to ink. Belt-and-suspenders alongside the explicit segmented migrations.

Language detection now defaults to ON for new installs. Previously read via UserDefaults.standard.bool(forKey:) which conflates "off" with "unset" — Hebrew transcripts on a default-English model were noticeably worse. Existing users who explicitly turned it off keep that choice.

item.title: Version 0.10.4.1 — Transcript window hotfix
item.description:
Hotfix: transcript window opens at the right size

v0.10.4 shipped with a regression: opening any non-trivial transcript produced a window much taller than the screen, hiding the resize handle. The clamp from the prior fix wasn't actually doing anything — NSHostingView's default sizingOptions propagated SwiftUI's full preferred height up to the window after the explicit setContentSize call had already run.

Two-line fix: clear sizingOptions on the hosting view so SwiftUI's preferred size never propagates back; set contentMaxSize as an upper auto-resize bound the user can still drag past via the resize handle.

Verified: a transcript that previously reported 880×3725 on a 1512×982 display now opens at exactly 880×720.

item.title: Version 0.10.4 — Window chrome system
item.description:
Kera Identity v3 — window chrome system

Every Kera window now reads as a single document: paper ground everywhere, centered floating titles, hairline structure, 8% ink wash for selection. Light and dark both supported.

  • All 6 windows unified — Settings, Activity Log, Permissions Setup, Library, Speakers Library, Speaker Editor, Transcript Reader. Transparent titlebar, paper bleeds up, centered title floats on the new chrome band.
  • "Library" — Meeting Library renamed to "Library" per the design handoff. The "Import audio" button now lives in the SwiftUI title row instead of a separate AppKit titlebar accessory.
  • Filter chips, unified — Library and Speakers Library filter pills now share the same KeraSegmented control. Selected pills paint with kerInk; counts visible with monospaced digits.
  • Selection wash — list-row selection uses kerInk @ 8% across Settings, Speakers Library, and Speaker Editor.
  • Hairlines, not borders — every structural rule normalized to 0.5pt kerHair.

Other fixes

  • "Auto-name with AI" → "AI Naming & Summaries" — toggle label now reflects that the setting also gates v0.10.3's library AI summaries, not just auto-naming.
  • Transcript window sizing — clamped initial frame to screen so transcripts no longer open larger than the display; cascade offset preserved.

Plan rivaled across 20 rounds (converged at 2 consecutive clean rounds); code rivaled across 1 round, catching 4 layout/contract bugs the plan-level review hadn't seen.
